note: Register of periodic processes on the host during a session (protocol v5, proposal 5.6; lead's answer to Q4). The fields of lab/periods.json. Nominal values from the source lines, none measured yet: G2 measures the real periods. scripts/tests/test_host_periods.py finds every Restart=, RestartSec=, timer and waiting loop in the sources listed here and fails on one this register does not name at its line. A process-creating entry that is active is bounded or has a random delay. random_s: the range added to period_s; period_s null: no fixed period (one round after another, or event driven). The collection grid is the reference entry; the host's timers outside the repository cannot be registered from source and are recorded at the start of every schema-3 session instead.

periods.name: collection grid
periods.note: Reference entry: vmicollect starts a snapshot every interval_s (5 s, protocol v5) on a fixed grid (decision D11); every other period is read against it. schedule.align is off (vmicollect/src/config.c), so the grid's phase follows the collector's start.

periods.name: drift of the two collectors' grids
periods.source: system: two vmicollect processes, one per VM, started independently
periods.note: The two collectors of concurrent sessions sample on grids of the same period with phases of their own start; their mutual phase is recorded per pair of concurrent sessions by package B9 (the audit records each grid's phase, grid_phase_s).

periods.name: host timers outside the repository
periods.source: system: systemd timers of the system manager and of the VM owner's user manager
periods.bounded: outside the repository: recorded at the start of every schema-3 session (systemctl list-timers --all of both managers, session.json host_context.timers); the owner disables the host timers during campaigns
periods.note: Cannot be registered from source (lead's answer to Q4); the record at session start is the evidence, never a reason.

periods.name: kernel dirty-page writeback
periods.note: The kernel writes dirty pages back every dirty_writeback_centisecs (default 500, 5 s) on a grid of its own; every page-cache write of the host (collector, traffic logs, monitor) is flushed by it. Outside the repository: G2 reads the value from /proc/sys/vm and measures its effect on the collector's cycle time.

periods.name: session records retry: patterns
periods.note: Encloses the retry below; at session start, before the measured phase.

periods.name: session records retry: files
periods.note: Encloses the retry below; at session start.

periods.name: session records retry
periods.note: Only while another VM's runner rewrites a session.json; reads files, at session start.

periods.name: preflight health wait
periods.note: GET /healthz with urllib until 200, before the warmup.

periods.name: warmup wait
periods.note: Checks that the generator and the monitor still run.

periods.name: capture loop of the runner
periods.bounded: events only: labctl event start and stop at the planned times, drawn continuously per session (plan of package B4)
periods.note: Every second: the children polled and the disk reserve checked; every 15 s /proc is read for a foreign generator; no process except the labctl calls of planned events. Ends with the collector.

periods.name: traffic worker loop (closed loop)
periods.note: Profiles lab and legacy only: a pause of 0.15 to 0.6 s after a burst, 0.5 to 1.5 s otherwise, HTTP requests only. Under schema 3 the v5 profiles run instead (package B5b, generator of agent T: its loops are registered when it is merged).

periods.name: traffic main loop
periods.note: Applies pending signals every SIGNAL_POLL_S (0.2 s) and writes the status file every summary interval (5 s, the collection period; a small file replaced, no process).

periods.name: traffic log writer
periods.note: The generator's single log writer: waits up to 1 s for a record (queue.get with a timeout) and flushes both traffic logs to the page cache every second; no fsync during the run (only at its end, like the host monitor), so it adds no synced write at the collection period on the collector's disk (finding F1 of the B5b verification).

periods.name: traffic log back-pressure
periods.bounded: only while the log queue is full
periods.note: A request record waits for room in the full log queue, retrying every 0.5 s; never a drop. The blocked time is in the end record (log_backpressure_s).

periods.name: v5 generator scheduler loop
periods.note: One round per due item: the next planned arrival (non-homogeneous Poisson process, proposal 5.3) or the next step of a user session (exponential think time); no fixed period, no process.

periods.name: v5 generator scheduler wait
periods.note: Inside a scheduler round: waits on its condition until the earliest due item or a reply; it ends when every arrival was offered and every user session is done (no user session arrives after --dur).

periods.name: host monitor sampling
periods.note: One sample of /proc per --interval-s (1 s from scripts/collection.py) on a fixed schedule; late ticks are skipped and counted.

periods.name: host monitor wait
periods.bounded: until the next sample is due
periods.note: Sleeps in steps of at most 0.2 s to the next tick.

periods.name: old traffic generator unit restart
periods.bounded: StartLimitBurst=5 within StartLimitIntervalSec=60, then the unit stays failed
periods.note: Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5: the collection period. User unit of labctl traffic-start and up (schemas 1 and 2, make lab-up); refused under a protocol of schema 3, and scripts/collection.py stops it before every session.

periods.name: guest agent retry
periods.bounded: 3 tries of an idempotent agent command (AGENT_RETRIES 2)
periods.note: One virsh qemu-agent-command per try, a pause of 2 s after a failed one.

periods.name: guest command poll
periods.bounded: the command's timeout (120 s; 180 to 240 s for an event)
periods.note: One virsh qemu-agent-command (guest-exec-status) about every 0.3 s while a guest command runs: event start and stop, state, clock, segment and journal (also during the other VM's measured phase).

periods.name: guest agent wait at start
periods.note: guest-ping through virsh after a VM start, between groups only.

periods.name: reboot wait
periods.note: labctl reboot only: virsh agent calls until a new boot id answers.

periods.name: QEMU swap read-back
periods.note: Reads memory.swap.max after the scope job, at VM start only.

periods.name: lab health wait
periods.note: GET /healthz with urllib (labctl health, deploy, up, status).

periods.name: libvirt session daemon wait
periods.note: Only when a VM start replaces or starts the daemon unit (Lab.daemon_step, way 1 of the swap ban): until the daemon of the pid file runs in hyptcn-libvirtd.service and accepts connections; it reads the pid file and probes the socket, no process.

periods.name: preflight order wait
periods.note: The preflight check of every session start waits for the worker to complete its order; HTTP only, beside the other VM's measured phase.

periods.name: campaign audit lock wait
periods.note: WAIT_POLL_S: one audit or archive on the host at a time; tries a lock, no process.

periods.name: pilot archive estimate
periods.bounded: one zstd per raw image of the accepted pilot, one after another, once at campaign start
periods.note: Schemas 1 and 2: protocol v5 has no pilot (package B9 replaces the estimate).

periods.name: campaign child wait
periods.bounded: the stage timeout (a capture: warmup_s + cycles x interval_s + 300 s), so about 1900 rounds per session
periods.note: Polls its child every 2 s and checks the archive mount each round (guard_mount runs findmnt): a host process every 2 s on a fixed grid through every session, 2:5 against the collection period. Finding for package B9: a random delay or a mount check without a process (proposal 5.6).

periods.name: campaign role order wait
periods.note: WAIT_POLL_S: before the first group of a later role, until the other VMs finished the earlier roles; reads status files, between sessions.

periods.name: campaign session loop
periods.note: One session after another (collection.py run, audit, archive); encloses the attempt loop below.

periods.name: campaign attempt loop
periods.bounded: MAX_ATTEMPTS 3 attempts of a session that ended before its measured phase
periods.note: RETRY_PAUSE_S (60 s) between attempts; each attempt starts scripts/collection.py run.
